_doc: Ratchet allowances for the plugin-kernel migration guardrails.
A guardrail fails when the current violation count EXCEEDS its allowance.
Allowances may only be lowered, never raised. Target for every key is 0.
Numbers recorded at P0 (baseline-1.7.0) unless noted. See docs/migration/.
_shimPages_note: One-line forwarding shims in a plugin-owned tree ('fake pluginization'). P5.2 reached the target: all 61 page shims became the real implementations, and 1 misfiled duplicate shim was deleted because no route imported it. src/pages/Student is now empty and src/pages/Teacher holds only the 5 pages that never had a shim.
_deadCode_note: Application-unreachable files. P4.3b.6 lowered this 65 -> 64 by deleting api/modules/pet (10 files, of which 1 was counted): its 17 routes moved into plugins/pet, so the module became unreachable rather than merely unused. Workspace cleanup lowered 64 -> 58 by deleting 6 genuinely-orphaned entries from this list (src/hooks/useTheme.ts, src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx, src/features/admin/api/adminAdapters.ts, src/features/admin/hooks/useAdminCms.ts, src/features/engagement/hooks/useCertificates.ts, src/hooks/queries/useTeacherPets.ts) plus one unlisted shim; ErrorBoundary's planned P5 revival is cancelled, so it must be re-added deliberately if ever remounted. P4.3b.6b deleted api/modules/classroom and api/modules/learning (8 files) and the three shared services they were the last consumers of (api/services/pointsService.ts, studentService.ts, featureService.ts - the point helpers now live in plugins/classroom, the 19 legacy enable_* gates in the capability system): the count moves 58 -> 69 -> 61 -> 58 as each layer stops being imported, and lands back on the same ceiling. featureService.ts was P7's stated target; it turned out to be unreachable the moment its last importer left, which is the right time to delete it. P4.3b.10 raised it 58 -> 59: migrating the engagement domain left `src/features/engagement/api/praisesApi.ts` with no importer (its only consumer was a hook deleted in the earlier workspace cleanup), so the frontend api module joined the list. That is the same shape as the previous round's finding - a domain migration can raise this number when it removes the last reference to a file nothing else used - and the honest response is to record the file rather than delete it on the way past, because it is P7's cleanup list, not this migration's.
_staticPluginRoutes_note: Static plugin-owned imports in the route entry file. P5.2b reached the target: AppRoutes.tsx is now a renderer over src/app/routing/routeTable.ts, and page modules are looked up in a map generated from that table, so the route layer never names a plugin module. Target reached - this must stay 0.
_legacyFeatureKeySurfaces_note: Files that hardcode a list of the legacy class feature keys. P4 removed the backend copy by deriving the names from the class row and moving the catalogue into the classroom plugin manifest. P5 removed the frontend copy the same way: src/lib/classFeatures.generated.ts is generated from plugins/classroom/plugin.json by `npm run class-features`, and G13 verifies it is up to date. Target reached - this must stay 0.
_adoptedTables_note: P3: plugins that own a table still carrying its legacy name (see PluginDataDeclaration.adopted). Grown by design across P4.3b as domains migrate: classroom 2, economy 3, dungeon 1, gacha 3, slg 2, battles 1, challenge 2, collaboration 5, marketplace 4, portal 3 = 26; P4.3b.5 added system 2 (question_bank, system_settings) = 28; P4.3b.5b added assignments 4 (assignments, student_assignments, exams, student_exams) = 32; P4.3b.5d added parent-buff 1 (parent_activity) = 33; P4.3b.6 added pet 1 (`pets`) = 34. The pet entry is the one increment that did NOT add a new table to the system: `pets` was already the domain's storage, and the P3 reference table it replaced (`p_pet_pets`) was invented and empty. Every entry is renamed to p_<slug>_ by P7 (target 0). Permanently-shared tables (currently `records`) are EXCLUDED and checked separately, as is the one shared-WRITE table (`redemption_tickets`) - see the SHARED_WRITE_TABLES set in plugin-manifest-conformance.test.ts. The ratchet's real guard is that this cannot grow except by migrating another domain, so every increment is enumerated here by hand. P4.3b.6b added learning 16 = 50: knowledge_edges, knowledge_nodes, paper_answers, paper_assets, paper_items, paper_sections, paper_submissions, papers, question_knowledge, questions, rubric_points, study_plan_items, study_plans, subjects, wrong_question_attempts, wrong_questions. That set is exactly the tables the migrated code reads or writes, measured against the deleted api/modules/learning service rather than guessed; the sibling tables in the same schema cluster (rubric_point_scores, knowledge_products, notes, note_assets, note_products) are deliberately NOT claimed because no route in the plugin touches them - claiming them would inflate this ratchet and misstate ownership. P4.3b.7 added identity 3 = 53: users, activation_codes, activation_events. These are the first entries that make an *existing, previously unowned* table owned - the boot schema created them and api/modules/auth wrote them through Prisma, so before this the ownership check had nothing to check on them, and api/modules/admin still writes them that way. P4.3b.8 added payment 2 = 55: payment_orders, payment_transactions - the two tables that had no table at all until P4.3b.5c created them from prisma/schema.prisma, which is why every /api/payment route answered 500 on a boot-schema database before that. With them, every table the payment routes touch has an owner. P4.3b.10 added engagement 10 = 65: announcements, certificates, class_announcements, danmaku_messages, family_tasks, lucky_draw_config, messages, praises, redemption_tickets, user_achievements. The last two are the two HANDOFF section 8.9 called ownership problems: `redemption_tickets` is the documented SHARED_WRITE_TABLES exception (marketplace issues tickets too, and that is named in the manifest rather than hidden), and `user_achievements` is the store behind the message feed's `sender_title`, claimed by nobody else. This is the last increment from a domain migration: admin and insights own no tables of their own that a plugin could adopt under a new name.
_routeCollisions_note: METHOD+PATH pairs served by more than one controller file. Invisible to the surface snapshot because it compares sets, and only the first registration is reachable. Peaked at 33 mid-migration (every plugin whose legacy module still existed), fell to 1 in P5.3b, and reached the target in P4.3b.6: the last one was plugins/pet vs api/modules/pet on GET /api/pet/students/:studentId, which could not be fixed by deleting the module because the plugin was not an equivalent replacement (4 endpoints, invented tables). P4.3b.6 ported all 17 legacy routes onto the real `pets` table and deleted the module. P4.3b.6b repeated the exercise for two more domains at once (classroom 47 pairs, learning 24, peak 71 while both legacy modules were still registered) and returned to 0 by deleting api/modules/classroom and api/modules/learning. This must stay 0 - a new collision means a domain is registered in both places again, and the way to fix it is deleting the legacy module, never raising this number.
